articles.title: Sara Ali Khan and Amrita Singh lease out 2,545 sq ft Mumbai office for Rs 3.76 crore over five years, with starting rent of Rs 5.85 lakh, deal includes 5% annual hike - Report
articles.summary: Sara Ali Khan and her mother, Amrita Singh, have leased a commercial office space in Mumbai’s Andheri West to artificial intelligence studio company
articles.body: Sara Ali Khan and her mother, Amrita Singh, have leased a commercial office space in Mumbai’s Andheri West to artificial intelligence studio company Upsurge Labs LLP for a five-year term. According to property registration documents reviewed by CRE Matrix, the deal has a total rental value of Rs 3.76 crore. The agreement includes an initial monthly rent of Rs 5.85 lakh, three car parking spaces and a 5% annual escalation.Sara Ali Khan and Amrita Singh’s Andheri West commercial property dealSara Ali Khan and Amrita Singh have rented out a 2,545 sq ft commercial office in the Signature building on Veera Desai Road, Andheri West, Mumbai. The property has a RERA carpet area of 2,545 sq ft and includes three car parking spaces. The leave and licence agreement was registered on September 29, 2026, for a period of 60 months. Upsurge Labs LLP, an AI studio company, is the tenant, with its partner Sowmay Jain representing the firm in the agreement.The five-year arrangement carries a total rental value of Rs 3.76 crore, as per the registration details reviewed by CRE Matrix.The agreement sets the initial monthly rent at Rs 5,85,350, while the security deposit stands at Rs 35,12,100. The lease commenced on October 1, 2026, with the tenant receiving a two-month rent-free period until November 30 to complete fit-out work. Rent payments are scheduled to begin on December 1, 2026. The agreement also provides for a 5% increase in rent every year over the five-year term.Based on the initial monthly rent and the stated carpet area, the rental rate works out to approximately Rs 230 per sq ft per month, before accounting for the annual escalation.No comment from Sara Ali Khan, Amrita Singh or Upsurge Labs yetThere has been no official response regarding the transaction from Sara Ali Khan and Amrita Singh.Saif Ali Khan’s commercial lease in Mumbai also made headlinesThe latest transaction follows news of a commercial property lease involving Sara Ali Khan’s father, actor Saif Ali Khan. According to CRE Matrix, Saif has leased two commercial units on Andheri Kurla Road, with a combined RERA carpet area of 5,692 sq ft. The agreement reportedly carries a monthly rent of Rs 22.76 lakh and was registered on September 29, 2026. The five-year lease covers the period from May 10, 2026, to May 9, 2031. The transaction adds to recent reports of commercial property activity involving members of the Khan family.Sara Ali Khan on work frontOn the professional front, Sara Ali Khan will be seen in 'Udta Teer', an upcoming Hindi spy action-comedy alongside Ayushmann Khurrana. Directed by Shashanka Ghosh, the film promises a blend of high-octane espionage and witty humor as the lead duo navigates an unexpected undercover mission. Originally slated to hit theaters on October 9, 2026, the makers pushed back the theatrical debut by two weeks. The spy entertainer is now scheduled to release in cinemas nationwide on October 23, 2026.Disclaimer: Figures presented in this article are derived from various public sources and are considered approximate unless explicitly noted. articles.title: Arshad Warsi to return as original Jolly in ‘Jolly LLB 4’ after Akshay Kumar headlined second and third instalments with Umesh Shukla to direct prequel that will wrap filming by January 2027 - Report
articles.summary: Arshad Warsi is set to return as the quick-witted lawyer Jagdish Tyagi, popularly known as Jolly, in the anticipated fourth instalment of the 'Jolly LLB'
articles.body: Arshad Warsi is set to return as the quick-witted lawyer Jagdish Tyagi, popularly known as Jolly, in the anticipated fourth instalment of the 'Jolly LLB' franchise. According to a recent report, the upcoming film will be an exciting prequel directed by Umesh Shukla, with filming expected to wrap by January 2027. The makers are yet to finalise the official title. The development marks Warsi’s return to the main lead role after Akshay Kumar headlined the second and third films, bringing the franchise back to the character who started it all.‘Jolly LLB 4’ to be a prequel starring Arshad WarsiThe Jolly LLB franchise is preparing to return with a fourth film, with Arshad Warsi leading the project under the direction of Umesh Shukla. Variety India has reported that the film is in production and is expected to complete its shoot by January 2027. The title is yet to be finalised, while the project is currently in the final stages of pre-production.A source quoted in the report clarified that the upcoming film will revisit the franchise’s past rather than continue the story after the third instalment. “The project is currently in the last leg of pre-production. And it’s not taking the film forward. It’s a prequel,” the source said.The first three films were written and directed by Subhash Kapoor. Shukla, who has directed films such as OMG: Oh My God! and 102 Not Out, will now take charge of the fourth instalment. Details about the plot, the setting and the supporting cast have not yet been officially announced.Arshad Warsi returns as the original Jolly after Akshay Kumar’s two instalmentsWarsi first played Jagdish Tyagi, the small-town lawyer known as Jolly, in Subhash Kapoor’s Jolly LLB in 2013. The film built its appeal around a lawyer navigating the legal system, combining courtroom drama with humour and social commentary.Akshay Kumar subsequently took over the lead role in 'Jolly LLB 2' and returned for 'Jolly LLB 3' as Jagdishwar Mishra, another lawyer known as Jolly. The third film brought the two characters together for a courtroom face-off, giving the franchise an opportunity to pit its original protagonist against its newer central figure.With the fourth film reportedly planned as a prequel, Warsi will once again lead the franchise. The timeline also creates the possibility of revisiting the character’s earlier days, although the makers have yet to disclose how the story will unfold.Will familiar faces from the first ‘Jolly LLB’ return?The franchise has built a recognisable supporting ensemble around its courtroom stories. Saurabh Shukla’s judge, whose interventions have provided both comic relief and a moral counterpoint to the lawyers’ arguments, has been a recurring presence. His return to the fourth film has not been officially confirmed in the information available so far.The original 'Jolly LLB' also featured Amrita Rao, Boman Irani, Mohan Kapoor and Sanjay Mishra. Whether any of them will reprise their roles in the prequel remains to be seen. The makers are yet to announce the complete cast or reveal whether the new film will retain the earlier instalments’ familiar courtroom setting.What does Umesh Shukla bring to the ‘Jolly LLB’ franchise?Shukla has previously directed 'OMG: Oh My God!', a social satire built around questions of faith and accountability, and '102 Not Out', a character-driven comedy starring Amitabh Bachchan and Rishi Kapoor. His filmography spans humour and stories that use familiar social situations to explore broader themes.‘Jolly LLB 3’ box office performanceThe third instalment, directed by Subhash Kapoor and starring Akshay Kumar and Arshad Warsi, brought the franchise’s two lawyers together for a courtroom confrontation. According to Sacnilk’s box-office tracking, Jolly LLB 3 collected approximately Rs. 117.50 crore net in India, with India gross earnings of Rs. 140.14 crore and overseas collections of Rs. 31.50 crore. Its worldwide gross stood at around Rs. 171.64 crore.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Shashi Tharoor calls Ranveer Singh's 'Dhurandhar' a propaganda film: 'I think Pakistanis will realise how much wrong has been done in their name'
articles.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor has shared his views on Aditya Dhar’s ‘Dhurandhar’ franchise after watching both instalments, which released in December 2025
articles.body: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor has shared his views on Aditya Dhar’s ‘Dhurandhar’ franchise after watching both instalments, which released in December 2025 and March 2026, respectively. While the Ranveer Singh-led films have emerged as major commercial successes, they have also drawn mixed reactions, with some viewers accusing them of promoting propaganda. Tharoor acknowledged the political messaging in the films but praised their storytelling, plot twists and cinematic execution, describing the latter as “brilliant.”In a video shared on his official YouTube channel, Tharoor said he enjoyed the second instalment more than the first. “As a work of fiction, as a work of entertainment, there is no doubt that the second part is superb,” he said. However, he was critical of the graphic violence depicted in the films, calling it “totally excessive and over the top.”“There was no need to show so much violence, blood, mayhem, cruelty and some of the most disgusting scenes ever seen in Indian cinema,” he added.Addressing the criticism that ‘Dhurandhar’ promotes propaganda, Tharoor acknowledged that the films contain elements of political messaging. He also referred to reports of the films being banned in several countries, including Pakistan and some Gulf nations.“There is a lot of propaganda stuff built into it obviously and I gather the film has been banned in many countries, not just in Pakistan, but many of the Gulf countries have banned it, saying it would needlessly create bad blood between Indians and Pakistanis, so I can understand those feelings.”Tharoor also reflected on how audiences in Pakistan might respond to the films, saying, “I don’t know how Pakistanis will react if they see this. Some of the lines, I think Pakistanis will laugh. Some of the other things, I think Pakistanis will realise how much wrong has been done in their name.”Since the franchise revolves around an undercover intelligence operative, Tharoor also compared the film’s portrayal of intelligence work with his own interactions with officials in the field. While he said he had dealt with several intelligence personnel, his experience had been considerably different from the cloak-and-dagger operations depicted on screen.“I have dealt with a lot of our intelligence people but in a very civilised way, having analysis, conversations, information exchanges but not really getting into any cloak and dagger stuff. I am certainly not aware of commands being given that lead to explosions in faraway capitals. That’s not the world I have ever lived in,” he said.The Congress MP also discussed R Madhavan’s character in the films, which is loosely based on National Security Advisor Ajit Doval. Tharoor questioned the plausibility of one person remaining in the same position from the late 1990s to the present, pointing out that such continuity would be unlikely in a bureaucracy. However, he understood why the filmmakers might have chosen to retain the same character to carry the story forward.“I think it would be too much of a stretch to assume that’s true. So I would see this as a fictional film that tells a story which obviously is meant to impart a certain sense of lessons as well,” he said.Despite his reservations about the violence and political messaging, Tharoor had considerable praise for the franchise's filmmaking. He described both films as “vividly made” and said they were “bound to have an impact on anyone who has an imagination or a mind.” He also appreciated the “competent acting” and “superb sort of sets, design, direction.”Summing up his experience of watching the two films, Tharoor concluded, “At the end of 8 hours, you feel you have been through a major cinematic experience.”The ‘Dhurandhar’ franchise has collectively earned over Rs 3,100 crore worldwide. Alongside Ranveer Singh, the two films feature Akshaye Khanna, Arjun Rampal, Rakesh Bedi, Sanjay Dutt, Sara Arjun and R Madhavan in key roles.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 2021, Reese Witherspoon sold a majority stake in Hello Sunshine at a $900 million valuation; five years later, she bought the company back
articles.summary: Reese Witherspoon has successfully bought back Hello Sunshine, her female-focused media company, at a fraction of its previous value. This follows her initial $900 million stake sale in 2021. Discover the journey and challenges faced by the company in the evolving media landscape.
articles.body: Reese Witherspoon, over the years, has started a lot of her own ventures, which also include her company Hello Sunshine. Starting at the rise of the streaming boom in the industry, she wanted to have a space for female creators in the industry to thrive and grow. Years later, in a deal to bring in more funds for the firm, she ended up selling the majority stake for a USD 900 million deal. Now, years later, after partnering with another media conglomerate, Witherspoon is back in the ownership circle, with almost 100% of the stake back under her name.Here is a look into the company’s overall journey.In 2016, Reese Witherspoon started her own companyReese Witherspoon and Seth Rodsky, along with backing from Peter Chernin and Jesse Jacobs' The Chernin Group, came up with an entirely new company called Hello Sunshine, which was built with the aim of championing female-driven stories and creators in the media realm that was heavily male-dominated.At the beginning of its establishment, the company acquired book rights via Reese's Book Club and produced hit television and film adaptations. These productions included ‘Big Little Lies,' ‘The Morning Show,' ‘Little Fires Everywhere,' ‘Daisy Jones & The Six,' and ‘Where the Crawdads Sing.'In August 2021, Reese Witherspoon sold off the majority of the stakes in her companyBBC reported that despite the ongoing success of her firm, Witherspoon’s company sold off the majority of its stakes for a lucrative deal at the time. A private equity-backed venture led by former Disney executives Kevin Mayer and Tom Staggs acquired a controlling majority stake in Hello Sunshine. The deal was settled for a whopping USD 900 million. Witherspoon netted an estimated USD 120 million in cash after taxes and retained an equity stake while staying on as a board member and producer.However, in the coming years, the overall valuation of independent productions dropped massively, and companies and platforms started pulling back on licensing budgets, third-party content spend, and overall production volume. Another major issue that dropped the overall valuation was the 2023 SAG-AFTRA and WGA strikes, which halted development pipelines across the industry. This, in turn, strained independent production entities even more, especially when most of them were dependent on overhead fees and greenlights.In October 2026, Reese Witherspoon bought back 100% of the companyOnly a few days ago, Variety reported that a European independent studio giant co-founded and led by CEO Pierre-Antoine Capton worked together with Reese Witherspoon to buy back her production company. The deal was estimated to be worth millions of dollars; however, the overall valuation is said to have been much less than what it was bought for earlier in 2021.Talking to The Wrap about the deal, the ‘Legally Blonde’ actress shared, “Mediawan has built a global, independent studio by putting creators first. That has always been my vision for Hello Sunshine. I'm investing alongside Mediawan and joining Pierre-Antoine Capton and his teams because this is the perfect home for this new media landscape.”While Witherspoon now has 100% under her name, the European conglomerate now also has access to all of the creative decisions that come under the firm’s future projects.DISCLAIMER: Figures presented in this article are derived from various public sources and are considered approximate unless explicitly noted. articles.title: D’Leesa, a cantora de 21 anos que viralizou fazendo tudo sozinha: 'Gravava no carro da minha mãe' | G1
articles.standfirst: Artista de 21 anos produz músicas e vídeos em casa, viralizou no TikTok e tem o Brasil como segundo maior país de ouvintes. Veja entrevista com o g1.
articles.summary: Artista de 21 anos produz músicas e vídeos em casa, viralizou no TikTok e tem o Brasil como segundo maior país de ouvintes. Veja entrevista com o g1.
articles.body:
D'Leesa no videoclipe de 'Hell or High Water' — Foto: Reprodução/YouTube

A cantora americana Cassidy D’Leesa Dzoole, conhecida como D'Leesa, é um fenômeno orgânico da internet como não se via há algum tempo.

Aos 21 anos, a artista de Atlanta, na Geórgia, faz tudo no estilo "do it yourself": é cantora, compositora, produtora, faz a mixagem e dirige os próprios videoclipes.

Sem grandes orçamentos ou produções, conquistou público em vários países — inclusive no Brasil, onde ela virá pela primeira vez para os festivais Batekoo (no dia 14 de novembro, em São Paulo) e No Ar Coquetel Molotov (no dia 28 de novembro, no Recife) .

Em entrevista ao g1 , por texto, D'Leesa contou que começou gravando os vocais no carro da mãe, usando o microfone dos fones de ouvido, e montava tudo no GarageBand. A artista conta que sempre gostou de compor, desde os 6 anos, mas parou na adolescência.

"Durante a adolescência, fui pressionada a seguir a carreira de STEM [Ciência, Tecnologia, Engenharia e Matemática], então parei de fazer música. Depois que me formei no ensino médio, em 2023, me senti com mais liberdade para explorar meus interesses", diz.

Só em 2025 ela comprou um microfone profissional. Foi também nesse ano que passou a usar as redes sociais para divulgar as músicas. "Eu filmava vídeos no meu quarto e postava no TikTok, no YouTube e no Instagram quase todo dia. Isso me ajudou muito a encontrar um público".

D'Leesa define o próprio estilo como "soul sáfico suave": músicas etéreas, às vezes dançantes, com letras sobre amar mulheres . Além de cuidar de todas as produções e vídeos, ela montou um site para divulgar o trabalho e vender produtos, como músicas personalizadas e itens de merchandising. "Tudo o que lanço atualmente é desenvolvido por mim", explica.

Esse estilo autêntico, "do it yourself", rapidamente atraiu fãs. Em outubro de 2025, D'Leesa postou no TikTok um vídeo cantando a música "Higher" e percebeu que o alcance disparava.

"Foi numa noite, em 2025. O vídeo estava ganhando milhares de visualizações e seguidores por minuto, e dias depois fui colocada na playlist Fresh Finds, do Spotify. Foi aí que pensei: 'Uau, as pessoas gostam das minhas músicas'", contou.

Em sua maioria, os vídeos de D'Leesa podem não ser grandes produções, mas são repletos de recursos: brincam com diferentes fundos, efeitos, sempre com a artista em evidência. Assim, ela chama a atenção não só por suas ótimas músicas, como pela forma dedicada e genuína que promove o próprio trabalho.

Um ano depois, D'Leesa revela que viver de música deixou de ser apenas um sonho.

"Chegou a um ponto em que a música é uma fonte real de renda para mim, e consegui sustentar partes da minha vida com streaming, vendas diretas, shows e outras oportunidades ligadas ao meu trabalho. Ainda estou transformando isso em algo totalmente sustentável a longo prazo, mas deixou de ser um sonho e virou algo tangível, que me sustenta financeiramente".

A vinda ao Brasil faz parte da primeira turnê da vida da artista. O público brasileiro é o segundo que mais consome a música de D'Leesa, de acordo com a cantora.

"Percebi que tinha fãs brasileiros quando chequei as estatísticas no Spotify for Artists e vi que o Brasil era meu segundo país com mais ouvintes. Acho que minhas redes sociais me permitem ter um público internacional, e sou muito grata por isso", disse.

Ela se apresenta no Brasil nos festivais No Ar Coquetel Molotov e Batekoo. Sobre a preparação para a estreia nos palcos, a cantora disse: "Essa é minha primeira turnê e estou muito animada para conhecer meus ouvintes. Estou me preparando fazendo exercícios e cantando ao mesmo tempo. Também ensaio o show como se estivesse no palco."

Perguntada sobre o que espera da passagem pelo Brasil, ela resume: "Espero uma festa: uma celebração da música, da expressão queer e do amor."

articles.title: 'Hanuman Ansh' box office collection Day 75: Vishal Chaturvedi's film earns Rs 62 lakhs; worldwide gross reaches Rs 450.68 cr; Tuesday collection rises by 121.4%
articles.summary: 'Hanuman Ansh', directed by Vishal Chaturvedi, recorded a rise in box office earnings on its 75th day in theatres.
articles.body: 'Hanuman Ansh', directed by Vishal Chaturvedi, recorded a rise in box office earnings on its 75th day in theatres. The film collected Rs 0.62 cr across languages on Tuesday, October 20, according to Sacnilk. This marks a 121.4% increase over the previous day's collection of Rs 28 lakhs. Its worldwide gross has reached Rs 450.68 cr, while the India net collection stands at Rs 340.75 cr.'Hanuman Ansh' box office collection on Day 75The film generated its latest domestic earnings across 490 shows. The Hindi version contributed Rs 0.61 cr from 483 shows, while the Telugu version added Rs 1 lakh through seven shows. Its cumulative India gross collection has reached Rs 402.08 cr.The latest increase follows a fluctuating run during the film's 11th week. It collected Rs 0.15 cr on Friday before earning Rs 26 lakhs on Saturday. Sunday's collection rose to Rs 46 lakhs, but Monday's earnings dropped to Rs 28 lakhs.Language-wise collection and occupancyThe Hindi version remained the primary contributor to Tuesday's earnings. It recorded 33% occupancy across its shows, while the Telugu version registered 34%. The Hindi release arrived in theatres on August 7, 2026, and the Telugu version followed on October 9, 2026.The film recorded 28,430 footfalls on its latest day. Its performance across both languages has contributed to its cumulative domestic earnings, with the Hindi version accounting for nearly all of Tuesday's reported collection.Weekly box office performance'Hanuman Ansh' recorded its highest weekly earnings during the fifth week, collecting Rs 90.25 cr. The sixth week followed with Rs 80.25 cr, while the fourth week contributed Rs 61 cr. Its seventh-week collection stood at Rs 44.80 cr.The film subsequently experienced a decline in weekly earnings. The eighth week brought in Rs 29.20 cr, followed by Rs 10.60 cr in the ninth week. The tenth week registered a slight improvement, collecting Rs 11 cr.The opening weeks had comparatively lower collections. The first week earned Rs 1.08 cr, while the second week added Rs 40 lakhs. The third week then recorded Rs 10.40 cr, marking an increase before the film's stronger run in subsequent weeks.Day-wise box office collection| Day | Date | India net collection ||---|---|---:|| Day 71 (Friday) | October 16 | Rs 15 lakhs || Day 72 (Saturday) | October 17 | Rs 26 lakhs || Day 73 (Sunday) | October 18 | Rs 46 lakhs || Day 74 (Monday) | October 19 | Rs 28 lakhs || Day 75 (Tuesday) | October 20 | Rs 62 lakhs || Total India net collection | | Rs 340.75 cr |The film has accumulated Rs 48.60 cr in overseas gross collections. Combined with its domestic gross, this takes the worldwide total to Rs 450.68 cr. Its India gross stands at Rs 402.08 cr, according to Sacnilk.The film follows Lakshmi Narayan, a young boy living in pre-Independence India who loses his mother and leaves home in search of God. His journey across Northern India gradually transforms his life, leading him towards spiritual devotion and selfless service as Neem Karoli Baba.'Hanuman Ansh' is the first instalment in a planned trilogy inspired by 'Divine Detour: That Changed My Life', a book based on the life of Neem Karoli Baba. The film stars Shobhinaw Satyaa and Chandan Anand in the lead roles. Anil Rastogi, Purnima Tiwwari, Sugandha Malhotra, Bhagvandas Patel and Neha Paranjpe also feature in the cast. Directed by Vishal Chaturvedi, the film was released in India on August 7, 2026.DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and the data in this article are compiled from public and industry sources. articles.summary: 'Prahaar - The Ujjwal Nikam Story', starring Rajkummar Rao, recorded an improvement in box office collections on its fifth day in theatres.
articles.body: 'Prahaar - The Ujjwal Nikam Story', starring Rajkummar Rao, recorded an improvement in box office collections on its fifth day in theatres. articles.title: Salman Khan was original target in shooting, Tiger Shroff an ‘easy second choice’ for Lawrence Bishnoi Gang: Reports
articles.summary: Actor Tiger Shroff was allegedly not the original target of the three shooters, who are reported to be members of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.
articles.body: Actor Tiger Shroff was allegedly not the original target of the three shooters, who are reported to be members of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. As per the latest reports, the shooters were reportedly targeting Bollywood superstar, Salman Khan, but allegedly abandoned their plans owing to the security arrangements at his residence.Salman Khan and not Tiger Shroff was original targetAccording to reports in various news publications, the three shooters involved in Sunday's firing incident in Mumbai's Juhu area had reportedly conducted a recce at Khan's home in Bandra. However, the security arrangements there reportedly discouraged them from carrying out the planned attack.On the look out for a comparatively easier target, the attackers allegedly monitored Tiger Shroff's movements through his Instagram account, as well as posts and videos shared by his fans, according to sources cited by IANS. The shooters reportedly watched the actor making his exit, before opening fire as his car.The incident took place on a busy Sunday evening and was captured on video. Tiger, the son of veteran actor Jackie Shroff, escaped relatively unhurt, however, his driver and a bystander sustained injuries.Accused arrested in RajasthanFollowing the firing, the accused reportedly fled to Surat in Gujarat before boarding a train to Jaipur. Their alleged plan was to travel to New Delhi by bus and then escape to Nepal. However, Mumbai Police arrested three accused in Rajasthan's Kota in connection with the case.Two of the arrested men have been identified as Ritik, alias Roshan, from Begusarai in Bihar, and Rehan from Sonipat in Haryana. Police have registered a case under charges of attempted murder and relevant provisions of the Arms Act.According to police sources, Rehan was in contact with Anil Pandit, an alleged associate of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. Following the incident, a social media post and an audio message from individuals claiming links to the gang surfaced, with the group allegedly claiming responsibility for the firing. The messages reportedly demanded an apology from Salman Khan to the Bishnoi community and threatened people associated with the actor.Salman Khan-Lawrence Bishnoi disputeThe long-running hostility between Salman Khan and Lawrence Bishnoi is linked to the 1998 blackbuck poaching case in Rajasthan. The Bishnoi community considers the blackbuck sacred, and Salman has faced repeated threats over the years, including a firing incident outside his Bandra residence in April 2024.Anup Jalota says apology could end hostilityMeanwhile, singer Anup Jalota has said that Salman Khan should apologise to the Bishnoi community to help bring an end to the ongoing hostility. Speaking to IANS, Jalota said, "I am very saddened by this. There is only one way to stop all this. Salman Khan should apologize to the Bishnoi community."He added, "I have said this before. It is very important that the Bishnoi community, which has been hurt, should be apologized to otherwise, the Bishnoi community will continue to be hurt. Those who work with Salman Khan will be hurt, their families will also be hurt."Jalota further urged Salman to take a firm decision to resolve the matter. "So, why not make a firm decision to apologize to the Bishnoi community to end this all? This is what I want."Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘Yeah, I shouldn’t have done that’: A$AP Rocky jokes about how things are ‘hell’ at home after revealing Rihanna's return to the studio
articles.summary: A$AP Rocky shares humorous insights on the consequences of revealing Rihanna's return to the studio, calling life at home 'hell' as he reflects on teasing her new music.
articles.body: A$AP Rocky is sharing that he faced quite some consequences at home after teasing the possible release of new music from his beau, Rihanna. A few months ago, the 38-year-old rapper had teased that Rihanna was working on some new music. However, it seems that things seem to have gotten close to “hell” at home after his comments. Read ahead to know more about what the robber had to say about the situation.A$AP Rocky jokes about the consequences of revealing that Rihanna is back in the studioWhile attending the 2026 Academy Museum Gala, A$AP Rocky opened up about how it was at home after he commented on the possibility of Rihanna releasing new music. He joked, while talking to The Hollywood Reporter, about the situation that he had to face quite a few consequences after revealing that the singer was back in the studio.During the interview, he joked, “It was hell. Yeah, I shouldn’t have done that.” When the rapper was asked about whether he wished to clarify anything else about the situation, Rocky quickly denied, saying, “No, I’m going to mind my business.”What did A$AP Rocky say about Rihanna releasing new music?For context, earlier this year in August, while featuring on ‘The Jason Lee Show,' she shared that the ‘We Found Love’ singer had made her way back to the studio after quite some time. The comment had come to light after the show’s host had asked him about the fan-led speculations over whether family life and her business venture were the reasons behind not releasing new music. He had commented at the time, “Nah. She is in the studio right now. Yeah, I said it. Sorry, babe.” He continued at the time, “Bro, she's working. She is cooking, no funny s---,” further joking about the matter and adding, “Damn, I'm gonna get in trouble for this.”Rihanna released her last studio album, 'ANTI,' ten years ago. Since then, while she has dabbled in music and has released songs, there has been no major release from the star for years now. Earlier this month, while holding a TikTok Live for the release of some new products for her beauty brand, Rihanna teased that she has racked up quite a collection of unreleased songs. While talking about her unreleased music, she commented, “If there are 10 products in a vault, then I have at least 17 vaults,” which directly implies there are 170 unreleased songs from the ‘Needed Me’ star.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
